This book is the story of how that runtime became a multi-tenant SaaS — one operated service that governs many customer tenants — and then how it was hardened into something production-grade and made to run, unchanged, on two clouds. It follows the architecture from the tenant-resolution middleware that binds each request to a tenant, through the per-plan quotas, rate limiting, audit trail, and standardized error surface that make a shared plane safe, to the passwordless data tier that removes the last long-lived secret on both Azure and AWS. The result is one plane that reconciles an estate spanning tenants and cloud boundaries, governed by one engine, reachable through whichever cloud door a program standardized on."

::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_26 — OrgPath as a Multi-Cloud Governance SaaS
:::


::: {.callout-note}
For thirty years, identity governance was something an organization did inside its own walls. UIAO started the same way — a single-tenant runtime an agency ran inside its own boundary. But the differentiated claim OrgPath makes is bigger than one boundary: it is that *one* reconciled organizational substrate can be governed across *many* tenants and *many* cloud boundaries by *one* runtime. This book is the engineering of that claim. It shows how the single-tenant runtime became a multi-tenant SaaS, how a shared plane is made safe to operate, how the last long-lived secret was removed from the data tier, and — the payoff — how the very same governance application runs unchanged on both Azure and AWS, because the part that is cloud-specific turns out to be small.
:::

## Companion canon

For the normative specifications this narrative paraphrases:

- [ADR-096 — Azure SaaS Architecture](/docs/adr/adr-096-azure-saas-architecture.html) — the multi-tenant control plane, per-request tenancy, and the stamp pattern; the foundational canon for this book.
- [ADR-115 — SaaS Production-Readiness](/docs/adr/adr-115-saas-production-readiness.html) — per-plan quotas, rate limiting, the control-plane audit trail, RFC 9457 problem+json, and the readiness probe.
- [ADR-116 — Azure Deployment Hardening](/docs/adr/adr-116-azure-saas-deployment-hardening.html) — passwordless Entra Postgres authentication and the IaC validation gate.
- [ADR-117 — AWS SaaS Surface](/docs/adr/adr-117-aws-saas-surface.html) — the AWS deployment on ECS Fargate + RDS via CDK, with passwordless RDS IAM authentication.
- [Architecture Decision Records](/docs/adr/index.html) — the binding record; this book is governed primarily by ADR-096, ADR-115, ADR-116, and ADR-117.
